title: Finite sets have affine neighbourhoods over an affine locally quasi-finite target
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $Y$ affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose $f$ is separated, meaning its diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product], and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. For every finite subset $E\subseteq |X|$, there is an affine open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] containing $E$. No quasi-compactness, Noetherianity or finite-type hypothesis on $X$ is imposed; $E=\varnothing$ and $X=\varnothing$ are allowed.

proof.text: If $E=\varnothing$, take the empty open subscheme of $X$. It is affine: the basic open $D_Y(0)$ in the given affine scheme $Y$ is empty (every prime contains $0$) and affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b); all empty open subschemes have the same empty structure sheaf. This includes $X=\varnothing$. Henceforth enumerate $E=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$ with $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine, applied to 0; empty case of Tag 07S0.

proof.text: For each $x_i$, choose an affine open $U_i\subseteq X$ containing it by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Put $U=\bigcup_{i=1}^n U_i$. Each $U_i$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Any open cover of $U$ restricts to a cover of each $U_i$; taking their finitely many finite subcovers gives a finite subcover of $U$. Thus $U$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme containing $E$.

source.place: Tag 07S0, lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-over-affine, first sentence of proof; affine basis Tag 01IT.

proof.text: Write $h=f|_U:U\to Y$. It is locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens], using the target open $Y$ itself. It is separated: the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies the pullback of $\Delta_f$ along $U\times_YU\to X\times_YX$ with $\Delta_h:U\to U\times_YU$. Indeed a test morphism to this pullback is a pair of maps into $U$ with identical images in $X$; the open inclusion is a monomorphism by [def-weil-open-immersion], so the two maps into $U$ coincide. Since $\Delta_f$ is closed, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes $\Delta_h$ closed.

source.place: Tag 01JY, lemma-base-change-immersion, applied to the restricted diagonal; local quasi-finiteness: Morphisms Tag 01TH, lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize (4).

proof.text: The affine scheme $Y$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $U$ is quasi-compact, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $h:U\to Y$ quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type], $h$ is locally of finite type. Thus $h$ has all four hypotheses of [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism-of-quasi-finite]: separated, quasi-compact, locally quasi-finite and locally of finite type. That lemma makes $h$ quasi-affine. By [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], evaluating at the affine open $Y$ shows that $U$ is a quasi-affine scheme: there are a ring $A$ and an isomorphism $j:U\xrightarrow{\sim}O$ onto a quasi-compact open $O\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Tag 07S0, second sentence, applying Tag 02LR, lemma-quasi-finite-separated-quasi-affine; quasi-compactness over a quasi-separated target: Schemes Tag 03GI.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p_i=j(x_i)\in O\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i), choose $a_i\in A$ with $\mathfrak p_i\in D(a_i)\subseteq O$. Set $J=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. For each $i$, $a_i\in J\setminus\mathfrak p_i$, so $J\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] to these $n\geq1$ prime ideals to obtain $a\in J$ lying in none of them. Then $j(E)\subseteq D(a)$. If $\mathfrak q\notin O$, all $a_i$ belong to $\mathfrak q$ because $D(a_i)\subseteq O$; hence $J\subseteq\mathfrak q$ and $a\in\mathfrak q$. Therefore $D(a)\subseteq O$. This writes out the finite-set shrinking inside the ambient affine scheme.

source.place: Tag 00DS, lemma-silly, its first slogan and prime avoidance statement; Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology. This is the direct proof of case (1) of Properties Tag 01ZY used by Tag 07S0.

proof.text: The principal open $D(a)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b). Set $W=j^{-1}(D(a))\subseteq U$. Since $D(a)\subseteq O$, the isomorphism $j:U\cong O$ restricts to an isomorphism $W\cong D(a)$, so $W$ is affine. Moreover $E\subseteq W$, and $W$ is open in $X$ because it is open in the open subscheme $U$. Its structure sheaf is the restriction of $\mathcal O_X$, as follows directly from [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus $W$ is the required affine open subscheme of $X$.

source.place: Tag 07S0, final sentence; affineness of a principal open: Schemes Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07S0, lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-over-affine; final invocation of Properties Tag 01ZY expanded using the elementary affine special case of Algebra Tag 00DS (first slogan).
